response.title: Does leaving a power station plugged into the wall all the time while running things through it wear out the battery?
response.answer:
Yes, leaving a portable power station plugged into the wall 24/7 while powering devices can accelerate battery degradation. However, how much depends heavily on the power station's design and whether it supports true AC bypass.

Two common scenarios

1. Power station with AC bypass (best case)

Wall outlet

Your devices

Battery stays charged, mostly idle

Wall power directly supplies connected devices.

The battery is not continuously charged and discharged.

Battery cycle wear is minimal.

However, keeping the battery at 100% for months can still accelerate calendar aging.

2. Power station without true bypass (more wear)

Wall

Battery

Devices

Battery participates in delivering power

The battery may experience frequent small charge/discharge cycles.

This can increase battery wear.

The amount of degradation depends on the charging system and battery chemistry.

How to minimize battery degradation

Feature

	

Recommendation




Battery chemistry

	

LiFePO4 (LFP) preferred




AC bypass

	

Use it if supported




Charge limit

	

70–80% for daily plugged-in use, if configurable




Temperature

	

Keep cool and ventilated




UPS/EPS mode

	

Fine for continuous use if manufacturer supports it

One important distinction: Even with true AC bypass, keeping an LFP battery at 100% continuously can cause more aging than keeping it around 80%. It is generally less concerning than repeatedly cycling the battery, though.

What power station do you have?

For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, DELTA Pro, Jackery Explorer 1000, or BLUETTI AC180.
